nodes.name: Electrosynthesis of CoFe-LDH Arrays
nodes.procedure: Hierarchical CoFe-LDH nanoplatelet arrays (250-300 nm in lateral length and ~8 nm in thickness) were synthesized on the surface of foam nickel substrate via a facile electrosynthesis method to form an interconnected network with open and porous structure.
nodes.source_text: The hierarchical CoFe-LDH nanoplatelet arrays were synthesized on the surface of foam nickel substrate via a facile electrosynthesis method. As shown in Figure 1A...

nodes.name: Electrochemical Activation of LDH
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical activation (ECA) was performed using cyclic voltammetry (CV) at 100 mV s⁻¹ scan rate in 1 M alkali electrolyte (KOH, NaOH, or LiOH). Optimal activation achieved at 0-0.6 V vs SCE after 4 CV cycles, inducing phase transformation from Co²⁺(OH)₂ to Co³⁺OOH with hydrogen vacancy formation.

nodes.description: Li⁺ intercalation supercapacitor performance of ECA(0.6V)-CoFe-LDH
nodes.source_text: The capacitance calculated from the CV profiles of ECA(0.6V)-CoFe-LDH was 434 F g⁻¹ in 2 M LiNO₃ aqueous solution, which was 26 times larger than that of initial CoFe-LDH (16 F g⁻¹). From the GV discharge curves... exhibited a capacity of 153 mAh g⁻¹ at 2 A g⁻¹... much larger than that of initial CoFe-LDH electrode (6.2 mAh g⁻¹)... capacitive retention of 99% was obtained, and the electrode surface retained its original hierarchical architecture after 10,000 charge-discharge cycles

nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern showed typical peaks at 2θ 11.59° and 22.68°, which could be indexed to the (003) and (006) reflections of the LDH material (Figure 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows decrease in stretching of hydroxide group and interlayer carbonate; Co–OH band at 798 cm⁻¹ vanishes with appearance of O–Co–O at 568 cm⁻¹ indicating conversion from Co(OH)₂ to CoOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra showed that both the stretching of the hydroxide group and the interlayer carbonate species decreased gradually (Figure 3B), illustrating the reduction of the hydroxyl group in the CoFe-LDH host layers and the loss of the interlayer carbonate.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Co 2p₃/₂ XPS shows peak at 782.38 eV (Co²⁺) shifting to 780.08 eV (Co³⁺, 92.1 wt%) after ECA; O 1s transitions from OH⁻ (531.3 eV) to O²⁻ (529.5 eV); Fe 2p₃/₂ at 711.0 eV shifts ~0.5 eV lower.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3C, the initial CoFe-LDH displayed a Co 2p₃/₂ peak located at 782.38 eV, indicating the existence of Co²⁺. A new peak at 780.08 eV attributed to Co³⁺ arose after the ECA process... The content of Co³⁺ increased from 0.4 wt% to 92.1 wt% via XPS spectra.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4A displays the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) results of ECA-CoFe-LDH with various treatment potentials... a significant energy shift of 6.3 eV is seen between ECA(0.6V)-CoFe-LDH and unactivated CoFe-LDH.
